The function $f(x)$ is defined and differentiable on $[-10,6].$ The graph of ${f}^{′}(x),$ the derivative of $f(x),$ is shown above, where the area of the region between the graph and the $x$-axis is $13.$ Find the minimum value of $f(x)$ on the interval $[-10,6]$ given that $f(-10)=-2.$

${f}_{\text{min}}=$
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
According to the candidates' test, the minimum value of $f(x)$ on $[-10,6]$ must occur at a critical point or an endpoint of the interval.

**Step 1**: Find the critical points:

We see that ${f}^{′}(x)$ is defined everywhere on $x\in (-10,6),$ and ${f}^{′}(x)\ne 0$ on this interval. Therefore, the candidates are $x=-10,6.$

**Step 2**: Compute the value of $f$ for each candidate using the fundamental theorem of calculus:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(-10) & =-2 \\ f(6) & =f(-10)+{\int }_{-10}^{6}{f}^{′}(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =-2+13 \\  & =11\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 3**: Select the smallest value of $f$ from our candidates.

Comparing the values of $f$ found in step $2,$ we have

$$
{f}_{\text{min}}=min\{-2,11\}=-2.
$$

Therefore, the minimum value of $f$ is ${f}_{\text{min}}=-2,$ and the value of $x$ that minimizes $f(x)$ is ${x}_{\text{min}}=-10.$
